page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-64GB is a memory-optimized virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The x86_64 architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. No local storage or dedicated GPU resources are bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is poor, as shown by stress-ng benchmarks, but multi-core execution scales to average levels. Memory performance exhibits a similar split, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching an average of 833.5 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak at 32.5 GB/sec and 24.93 GB/sec respectively. Passmark memory testing also rates the memory subsystem as weak.

For application workloads, the instance delivers average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average tiers, processing 11.88 million operations per second. However, static web serving throughput is weak at 6.07 GB/sec. Large language model inference is viable for small 135M models but degrades to poor performance on medium 7B models.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for medium-sized databases, caching layers, and multi-threaded background processing tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 8 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs at 2.0 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Benchmark data shows poor single-core performance but average multi-core capabilities, with Passmark CPU and Geekbench scores sitting in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is average for cached small blocks but weak for uncached large blocks. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that tolerate shared CPU resources. It is best suited for database operations, Redis caching, and multi-threaded data processing.
